atropos.CacheBoxContext.description:
CacheBoxContext, when present, is authoritative end-to-end (design
doc Q3): its KeyStrategy/KeyHeaders/MissStatus take precedence over
CacheBoxKeyStrategy and the CacheBox's construction-time default.
Populated at rule-match time from the matched rule's compiled
cache-box context (or the freeze command's, for the freeze path).

id.description: slot identity (service+category:type); unused on compiled rules
slot identity (service+category:type); unused on compiled rules

host.description:
Host and Capture say which instrument host answered ("in-process" |
"sidecar") and, for the sidecar, how traffic reaches it ("explicit" |
"transparent").

stale_for.description:
StaleFor is the human-readable duration since LastSuccessfulPollAt.
Empty if never polled. Helps ops dashboards distinguish a 5s vs 5h DEGRADED.

direction.description:
Direction selects which half of a proxied connection to apply the
toxic to: "upstream" (client → server, request bytes) or "downstream"
(server → client, response bytes). It defaults to "upstream" with
Host=="proxy" and to "downstream" with Host=="inline".

host.description:
Host selects where the toxic runs.
  "proxy"  → TCP proxy (requires a NetworkResolver; the in-process default)
  "inline" → armed policy on the atroposd sidecar's proxied upstream calls
The in-process host has no proxied connection to shape: it skips a rule
with Host=="inline" (reported as unsupported) and rejects a single
/admin/fault slot with 400. An empty Host means "inline" on a host that
owns the proxied connections (the sidecar) and "proxy" in-process.

scope.description:
Scope is the fraction of connections (proxy) or requests (inline)
to which the toxic applies. Zero means 1.0 (all).

target.description:
Target is the logical name of the upstream service. Required for both
hosts. With Host=="proxy" a NetworkResolver turns it into a
(listen, upstream) address pair; with Host=="inline" it is the
upstream's host or host:port, matched against the outbound request's
host (a target without a port matches any port).

atropos.ReplaySetRef.description:
ReplaySet is the replay set desired on this instance: absent means no replay
set is desired, so the instance clears one it holds. Present, it names the
set to pull: ExperimentID and PhaseID are the (experiment, phase) pair it
is installed under (the cache-box serves it only to the rule whose context
matches that pair), ID is `sha256:<hex>` of the artifact bytes fetched from
URL, and SHA256 is the W5 digest over its entries.

url.description: relative to the manteion base URL

etag.description:
Etag is the ETag of this materialized document: a hash of its content
alone, never the generation (that travels in Version and in the
X-Atropos-Generation header), so an unchanged document keeps its ETag
while the generation moves. The instance treats it as opaque and sends
it back as `If-None-Match`.

version.description: the generation, kept under the old name

labels.description: all must match (AND semantics); empty = wildcard

cachebox.CacheBoxContext.description:
CacheBoxContext, when present, is authoritative end-to-end (design
doc Q3): its KeyStrategy/KeyHeaders/MissStatus take precedence over
CacheBoxKeyStrategy and the CacheBox's construction-time default.
Populated at rule-match time from the matched rule's compiled
cache-box context (or the freeze command's, for the freeze path).

cacheBoxKeyStrategy.description: legacy, construction-time-only hint; empty = default. Superseded by CacheBoxContext when present.

info.description:
Admin and health handlers exposed by the atropos-go SDK.
Serve mounts these on the returned handler at the documented
paths; the generated spec documents that control surface.
The manteion-protocol operations document the desired-state
endpoints the SDK calls (the poll and the status report);
manteion serves those, Serve does not mount them.
info.title: Atropos SDK Admin API

delete.description: Clears the record-side store and the installed replay set.

get.description: Store, recorder and record-buffer counters, plus the replay_with_delay source in force: whether a fitted source is installed, its mu and sigma, and the (experiment_id, phase_id) it is scoped to (both empty = every replay). The stats structs carry no JSON tags, so the response keys are the Go field names (Delay.Installed, Store.Entries, ...), not the camelCase names the response schema renders; the keys are a wire surface and stay as they are.

post.description: Installs a lognormal delay source for replay_with_delay. A context scopes it to its (experiment_id, phase_id): a replay under any other pair keeps sleeping the entry's observed latency, and without a context the source applies to every replay. A source installed here lasts until the next desired-state 200 answer without freeze_cfg clears it; a 304 leaves it.

400.description: malformed JSON, negative mu or sigma, or a context naming only one of experiment_id and phase_id

post.description: Installs a single demo/admin fault decision. Inline faults run in request flow; network and resource faults run in the background.

Applies the rule set through the single apply path the manteion sync also uses, scoped to rules: admin fault slots, the delay source and the installed replay set stay as they are. Rules this host cannot execute (a category outside its capabilities, quota resource faults in-process, network host=inline outside the sidecar or host=proxy without a resolver, compositions) are skipped per rule, logged and counted in atropos_rules_unsupported_total{category}; the rest apply and the answer is 204. A rule that does not decode is skipped and logged, not counted, and the answer is 422; the pushed set less the skipped rules replaces the installed one (an empty set when no rule decodes). Connected to manteion, a push is a short-lived override: it clears the ETag the instance holds, so the next poll is unconditional and its 200 re-applies the desired state over the pushed set, at most one long-poll hold plus the apply later; the push sends no status report. Offline, the pushed set holds until the next push.

204.description: rules replaced (rules this host cannot execute are skipped)

422.description: some rules did not decode and were skipped; the rest replaced the installed set (an empty set when none decoded); error joins the per-rule messages with '; '

500.description: hard error: this host cannot hold rules, nothing was applied

get.description: Served by manteion, not by Serve: the SDK is the client. version is the generation the instance holds, If-None-Match the ETag of the document it holds (sent only when it holds one), and wait (seconds) asks manteion to hold the request (the SDK sends 30): manteion holds it only when version is the service's current generation and the ETag matches, until the generation changes or the wait elapses, and answers a matching ETag with any other version (older, absent or zero, or ahead after a manteion database reset) 304 at once, carrying the current generation. The ETag is a content hash alone; the generation travels in X-Atropos-Generation and in the body's version. The SDK treats the ETag as opaque. 200 is applied through the single apply path and reported with POST /api/v1/sdk/status; 304 means the document is unchanged and the instance adopts the generation without applying.

parameters.description: ETag of the document the instance holds
parameters.name: If-None-Match

X-Atropos-Generation.description: generation of the desired state, to adopt

get.summary: Poll the desired state (served by manteion)

post.description: Served by manteion, not by Serve: the SDK is the client. Sent after every apply and whenever the replay-set state changes. The report is a full snapshot of what the instance holds: unsupported and errors replace the previous report (an empty list clears it), and replay_set names the desired replay set and its pull state (fetching and failed name a set not yet held, while an earlier committed set may still be installed): an absent replay_set means none is desired. Any 2xx counts as delivered (manteion answers 204); a report that fails to send is re-sent.
post.summary: Report the desired state held (served by manteion)

get.description: Synchronous, pull-based snapshot of everything needed to compute a phase's VALID/INVALID verdict from this instance (design doc Q6).
get.summary: Read per-(experiment, phase) cache-box fidelity counters

post.description: Clears any prior staging for (experiment_id, phase_id) and starts a new one.
Idempotent by chunk_seq -- redelivering the same chunk_seq does not double-count.

409.description: no active preload for this pair

post.summary: Append a chunk to a staged cache-box preload

post.description: Verifies count+checksum (wire spec §W5); on match, atomically installs the staged set as the replay set for the pair. On mismatch, staging is dropped and any previously installed set is left untouched.
